newsitem.title: USA: Republic to buy 2 Calif. solid waste companies.
newsitem.headline: Republic to buy 2 Calif. solid waste companies.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc., continuing its expansion in California, said Tuesday that it agreed to acquire solid waste companies that serve the Los Angeles and Long Beach areas.

Republic, which also said it finalised its acquisition of PSI Waste Systems Inc. of Twin Falls, Idaho, said it was acquiring Consolidated Disposal Service Inc. of Santa Fe Springs, which serves the Los Angeles area, and Bel-Art Environmental Services Inc. of Long Beach.

The Fort Lauderdale-based company, which operates a number of solid waste service companies throughout the country, said it would pay a total of $65 million worth of its stock to acquire the three companies. It did not provide individual purchase prices.
Republic said executives of all three companies will sign long-term employment agreements with Republic and will continue in their respective roles.

"The acquisitions of Consolidated and Bel-Art add significantly to Republic's solid foundation in southern California and provide a great strategic fit with Taormina Industries," Republic Vice Chairman Harris W. Hudson said in a statement.
"We are extremely pleased to welcome each of these companies into Republic and we look forward to expanding our businesses together."

Republic, which also owns the nation's largest chain of new-car dealerships and is building a chain of used-car megastores, acquired Taormina Industries Inc., a large waste and collection services company in Anaheim, Calif., in March.
Republic's stock gained $1.125 to $28.25 in morning trading on the Nasdaq market.
